newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambican businessman jailed on hashish charge.
newsitem.headline: Mozambican businessman jailed on hashish charge.

text.p: Mozambique's first major drug trafficking trial ended on Wednesday with an eight-year jail sentence for a businessman accused of being in possession of hashish.

The Maputo city court convicted 33-year-old Mozambican businessman Samssudine Satar for his involvement in a case involving two containers loaded with hashish which were seized by the police in a Maputo suburb in May 1995.

The hashish was disguised in packaging normally used for cashew nuts. Police claimed the haul weighed 40 tonnes but in court it was admitted that this was actually the capacity of the containers. The contents had not been weighed.
In recent years Mozambique has acquired a reputation for being a conduit for the international drug trade. The court decision is the first sign of a crackdown.
Judge Isabel Rupia sentenced Satar to seven years in jail for drug trafficking, and an additional one year for trying to bribe a policeman with 3.5 meticais (just over $300).

He must also pay the state over two billion meticais (about $174,000) in compensation for the expenditure incurred in destroying the hashish. Other fines and legal costs amount to 1.8 million meticais.
